title: Global pricing for the Redmi Note 17 series leaks - GSMArena.com news
summary: Leaked euro pricing for the Redmi Note 17 family suggests European retail tags ranging from €250 for the base 4GB/128GB Note 17 to €600 for the Pro Max 8GB/256GB. The leak also mentions a 108MP main camera and color options, but it's unclear which models get which specs. Global availability is expected in the coming weeks.
content:
The Redmi Note 17 and Redmi Note 17 Pro were launched in China earlier this month, and reports have suggested the standard model will land in India on August 6. The range is also headed to other markets, including Europe, and euro pricing for several global configurations has now leaked.

According to the leak, the Redmi Note 17 4G will be priced at €250 for the 4GB RAM / 128GB storage configuration, while a 6GB / 256GB variant would cost around €300. The Redmi Note 17 5G is listed at approximately €400 for the 6GB / 256GB model.

Higher-tier models carry steeper tags: the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G with 6GB RAM and 256GB storage is reportedly set at €500, and the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max 5G with 8GB RAM and 256GB storage is shown at about €600.

The source behind the leak also claims the global Redmi Note 17 will feature a 108MP main camera and be offered in black, blue, and purple finishes. The leak does not explicitly confirm whether the 108MP sensor applies to the 4G or 5G model; given previous patterns, observers assume it will be a feature of the higher-end 5G variant, but that has not been verified.

It remains unclear how the global lineup — which appears broader than the two-model Chinese release — will map onto the Chinese models in terms of hardware differences and naming. Regional variants, network compatibility, and software configurations could all diverge between markets.

If the global launch is imminent, OEM announcements and retailer listings should clarify the final prices, specs, and availability within a few weeks. For now, the leaked euro figures give a mid-range pricing picture that places the family competitively against other Android devices in the same segment.

Commentary on the leak from forum contributors noted that the Pro Max's price aligns it with some established mid-range competitors and suggested the tag isn't glaringly overpriced. Additional hands-on reviews and official confirmations will be needed to judge value relative to performance, cameras, and long-term software support.
